PS14-Simple-Blackjack/starter/README.md.content:
# Simple Twenty-One starter

Work with integer card values from 2 through 11. Deal two cards to each hand. Use h to draw, s to stay, or q to quit. A hand above 21 busts. The dealer draws below 17. Compare the totals when neither hand busts.

Use practice mode for a player hand of 10 and 7 and a dealer hand of 9 and 6. If the player stays, the dealer draws 3 and wins with 18. Replay the same mode to verify that neither hand carries over.

PS14-Simple-Blackjack/starter/main.py.content:
hand = [10, 7]
print(f"Player: {hand} = {sum(hand)}")

# Have the dealer draw below 17, then compare the final totals.

PS14-Advanced-Blackjack/starter/README.m.content:
# Named-Card Twenty-One starter

Count Jack, Queen and King as ten. Count every ace as one. If an ace is present and adding ten keeps the total at or below 21, add ten. Ace and 6 total 17, then Ace, 6 and 8 total 15. Use the same helper for each hand and have the dealer stop at a best total of 17 or higher.

In practice mode, hit twice and then stay. The player totals are 17, 15 and 19. The dealer draws from 16 to 18. Check dual two-card 21 as a tie.

PS14-Game-of-War/starter/README.md.content:
# High Card Rounds starter

Use values from 2 through 10. Compare two draws each round. Increment only one win count or the tie count, then report the overall winner or an overall tie. Wins and ties should add to ten.

Enter Ari and Bea as the names and p for practice. The fixed ten rounds produce Ari 4, Bea 3, ties 3. Press Enter instead of p to test random draws.

PS14-Mastermind/starter/README.md.content:
# Signal Digits starter

The signal has four digits from 0 through 5. Count exact matches first and set those positions aside. Count each remaining signal digit at most as many times as it occurs. For signal 2032 and trial 2230, expect two exact and two misplaced. Trial 2222 gives two exact and zero misplaced.

Give each round eight trials. A hint reveals the sum of the hidden digits and spends one trial. Invalid input uses none. Choose p to practice with 2032.

PS14-Mastermind/starter/main.py.content:
sample_signal = "2032"
sample_trial = "2230"
exact = 0

for signal_digit, trial_digit in zip(sample_signal, sample_trial):
    if signal_digit == trial_digit:
        exact += 1
print(f"Exact: {exact}")

# Count misplaced digits after removing the already-matched positions.
